title: Cougar Helicopters Flight 91

location.name: Atlantic Ocean, 35 nm east of St. John's

summary: Cougar Helicopters Flight 91, a Sikorsky S-92A on a regular shuttle flight to offshore oil platforms, reported zero oil pressure in the main gearbox at 09:40 NDT at cruise. The crew attempted return to St. John's but ditched 8 minutes later after losing electrical power. Of 18 aboard, one survived with serious injuries; the other 17 died of drowning. A broken titanium stud in the main gearbox oil filter assembly, subject of a prior Alert Service Bulletin, initiated the failure.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by a broken titanium stud in the main gearbox oil filter assembly that had been the subject of a prior Alert Service Bulletin recommending replacement within one year or 1,250 flight hours. The accident was contributed to by the fact that a previous similar incident in Australia in August 2008 involving total loss of oil and emergency landing did not result in industry action to correct the defect.

factors.evidence: Sikorsky issued Alert Service Bulletin on 28 January 2009 recommending replacement of titanium studs within one year or 1,250 flight hours; this defect had not been addressed on C-GZCH at the time of accident (p. 1-2)
Loss of oil pressure in main gearbox at 09:40 caused by broken titanium stud; total loss of oil in transmission (p. 1)
Prior incident in Dandenong, Australia August 2008 involved total loss of oil and emergency landing but defect was not corrected industry-wide (p. 149)
Crew attempted return to St. John's and ditched in Atlantic Ocean at 09:48; helicopter sank in 178 m water (p. 1)

17 occupants died of drowning in helicopter that capsized in cold water; water temperature was approximately 0°C preventing effective escape; occupants lacked supplemental breathing apparatus (p. 149-150)

events.text: Aircraft reported zero oil pressure in main gearbox at cruise altitude; crew issued mayday
Crew initiated emergency procedures for main gearbox oil pressure loss
Crew descended to 800 feet and turned toward St. John's International Airport
Aircraft lost electrical power due to continuing gearbox degradation
Crew prepared for emergency ditching; moved to ditching position heading
Aircraft ditched in Atlantic Ocean after losing electrical power; high rate of descent at impact
Helicopter capsized and sank in 178 m water; occupants struggled to escape in 0°C water
Provincial Airlines ice patrol airplane spotted aircraft floating upside down 25 minutes after ditching

recommendations.text: The Federal Aviation Administration assess the adequacy of the 30 minute main gearbox run dry requirement for Category A transport helicopters.
Transport Canada prohibit commercial operation of Category A transport helicopters over water when the sea state will not permit safe ditching and successful evacuation.
Transport Canada require that supplemental underwater breathing apparatus be mandatory for all occupants of helicopters involved in overwater flights who are required to wear a PTSS.
Rotorcraft manufacturers include run dry time information in rotorcraft flight manuals to assist pilots during MGB abnormal or emergency situations.

safety_changes: S-92A gearbox malfunctions section amended to include statement advising pilots that total loss of MGB oil pressure may result in MGB failure in less than 10 minutes
Increased focus on emergency underwater breathing apparatus (EUBA) requirements for offshore helicopter operations
Enhanced sea state criteria for helicopter ditching capability assessments

notes: TSB Aviation Investigation Report A09A0016 read in full
Sections read: Occurrence Summary, Safety Issues, Findings, Causal Factors, Safety Action
Four formal recommendations identified: A11-01 through A11-04
Defect causation clearly documented with prior Alert Service Bulletin SB 329-77-1004
Drowning was immediate cause of death due to cold water and helicopter orientation after impact
One survivor recovered; this was one of TSB's most significant offshore aviation accidents
